tagline: The first VALORANT Champions anthem, and still the one fans crown.
headline: Grabbitz's 2021 anthem gave VALORANT Champions its first theme song and became the benchmark every later anthem chases.
summary: Released on November 22, 2021, nine days before the first VALORANT Champions in Berlin, "Die For You" was written, produced and sung by Grabbitz and paired with an anime-style video by The Line in which Brimstone, Sage and Phoenix retake Split's B site from Chamber. It played between matches on the broadcast, lived inside the Champions 2021 Vandal and returned in remixes by Zedd and Dabin that both debuted live. Its video now has more than 122 million YouTube views, more than the five later Champions anthem videos combined, and many fans still rank it the best.

story.heading: An anthem for a league with no legends yet
story.body:
League of Legends had spent years building its Worlds anthem tradition when VALORANT's esports team set out to make one of its own. Work on the song began in October 2020, ahead of the VALORANT Champions Tour's first season. "The endgame for us has always been an anthem of some kind," Anton Ferraro, global communications lead for VALORANT Esports, told Upcomer, pointing to League anthems such as *Awaken*, *Warriors* and *Burn It All Down*.

There was a catch. VCT was in its first year and had no Faker-style icon to build a video around, so Riot made the anthem about the game itself rather than any team or player: the bond between players and the agents they control, and the way a single clutch round can decide a tournament. For the music, Riot looked for an artist whose sound fit VALORANT and chose Grabbitz, the Buffalo-born electronic producer and singer Nicholas Chiari, known for work with Pegboard Nerds, Savoy and deadmau5. Grabbitz wrote, produced and sang the track, and Eric J mixed and mastered it.

story.heading: One retake on Split
story.body:
The video was made with The Line, the animation studio behind League's *Take Over* video, and it turns a single round into a small epic. Chamber, then VALORANT's newest agent, guards a Spike already planted on Split's B site with his sniper rifle, while Brimstone, Sage and Phoenix push through smoke to retake it. As the retake goes wrong, the video pulls each defender into a dreamlike inner world where they come face to face with the player controlling them. Upcomer read these scenes as each agent's flaw: Brimstone can't give up command, Phoenix is reckless, and Sage is insecure about what she can't control. Each has to let go and trust their player.

The payoff is pure VALORANT. Phoenix comes back with his Run It Back ultimate, Sage heals Brimstone, Phoenix throws Sage the defuser, and agents and players blur together as the Spike is defused. Esports.gg's launch-day review praised both the song and the animation, and ONE Esports joked that Phoenix burning his ultimate out in the open was a reminder of every toxic Phoenix players had queued with.

story.heading: The sound of Berlin
story.body:
VALORANT Champions 2021 ran from December 1 to 12 in Berlin, with 16 teams competing for the first world title. Riot built the anthem into the whole event. It played in the broadcast's waiting room between matches, and the limited Champions Collection carried it into the game: inspecting the Champions 2021 Vandal played an instrumental version of the song, and the gun's finisher turned the map into a scene from the video, with a giant Brimstone looming overhead. The bundle also included player cards of Phoenix, Sage and Brimstone. Half of its revenue went to the qualified teams, and by December 8 it had raised more than $7.5 million for them.

Finals day, December 12, brought the first musical guests at a VALORANT event: Zedd, Rezz, PVRIS and Grabbitz. Zedd, who had made League's 2016 Worlds anthem *Ignite*, debuted his electro-house remix of *Die For You* with Grabbitz during the Finals Ceremony, and the remix was released the same day. Later that day Acend beat Gambit Esports 3–2 to become the first VALORANT world champions.

story.heading: Remixes and encores
story.body:
The song kept coming back. In July 2022, Dabin on guitar, Salin on drums and Grabbitz on vocals played the opening ceremony of VALORANT Regional League France: Révolution. The set ended with Dabin's then-unreleased melodic-bass remix of *Die For You*, which came out on July 8. At the Champions 2023 Grand Final opening ceremony at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles, where Riot expected more than 10,000 fans, Grabbitz walked out, sang a line of *Die For You* and went straight into that year's anthem, *Ticking Away*.

Riot has kept it at the center of the VALORANT catalogue. It is on the 2024 compilation *VALORANT Sounds, Vol. 1*, and in May 2025 the game's fifth-anniversary *5 Year Mashup* wove it together with *IGNITION*, *Karanlığın* and *Ticking Away*.

story.heading: The voice of VALORANT esports
story.body:
*Die For You* made Grabbitz the main voice of VALORANT esports. He co-wrote and produced *Fire Again*, the 2022 Champions anthem sung by Ashnikko, and in 2023 he co-wrote, produced and performed *Ticking Away* with bbno$. That year he told GamesBeat that the impact the songs had on the community and the players had been astonishing.

In 2026 he returned for Champions Shanghai with *If The Sun Burns Out Tonight*, alongside Bring Me The Horizon's Oli Sykes and Spiritbox's Courtney LaPlante. Coverage of the announcement noted that his first three VALORANT collaborations had passed 350 million streams worldwide.

story.heading: Still the one to beat
story.body:
Nearly five years on, the numbers back up its reputation. The official video has about 122.8 million views and 1.3 million likes. That is more than three times the next most-watched Champions anthem video, *Ticking Away* (39.4 million), and more than the five later Champions anthem videos combined (about 104.5 million). On Spotify, *Die For You* has about 184.9 million plays, more than double *Ticking Away*'s 81.8 million.

Fans agree. Looking back over every Champions anthem in 2024, Esports.gg called *Die For You* the one that started it all, said many still believe it is the best, and wrote that later anthems would have trouble topping it.

whyItMatters: It was the first VALORANT Champions anthem, bringing League's Worlds-anthem tradition to Riot's newer esport.
With no star players to build it around yet, Riot made it about the game itself: the bond between a player and their agent in a clutch round.

It ran through the first Champions: it played between matches, lived inside the Champions 2021 Vandal's inspect and finisher, and that Vandal headlined a collection that raised more than $7.5M for the 16 teams.
Its video is by far the most-watched Champions anthem, with about 122.8M views, more than the five later anthem videos combined.
It started Grabbitz's run as the voice of VALORANT esports: Fire Again (2022), Ticking Away (2023) and If The Sun Burns Out Tonight (2026).
It keeps coming back: Zedd and Dabin remixes that debuted live, Grabbitz's callback at Champions Los Angeles, the 2024 compilation VALORANT Sounds, Vol. 1 and the fifth-anniversary medley.

keyMoments.label: Title card on Split
keyMoments.description: The Die For You title card, credited to VCT x Grabbitz, appears over an empty garage entrance on Split, where the retake plays out.

keyMoments.label: The retake begins
keyMoments.description: An explosion fills the entrance with smoke, and Sage and Brimstone push through it toward the planted Spike.

keyMoments.label: Chamber takes aim
keyMoments.description: Chamber smirks behind his sniper rifle and fires, and a spent shell casing spins across the screen.

keyMoments.label: Brimstone's red void
keyMoments.description: As the chorus arrives, Brimstone is pulled into a blood-red void where he meets the player controlling him.

keyMoments.label: Under the black sun
keyMoments.description: A colossal black sun hangs over the red wasteland, and a giant Brimstone rises beneath it beside his tiny player and raises his fist. A giant Brimstone also appears in the Champions 2021 Vandal's finisher.

keyMoments.label: The drop
keyMoments.description: The beat drops as the black sphere plunges into the ground, and Brimstone's giant feet crash down around his player before his huge face looms over them.

keyMoments.label: Phoenix's trial
keyMoments.description: Phoenix drifts through a purple cosmos, soon holding a glowing orb, as the rapid-fire "Everything I know" section begins.

keyMoments.label: Phoenix ignites
keyMoments.description: Phoenix screams as flames engulf him, the start of a fiery sequence built around his reckless nature.

keyMoments.label: The face of fire
keyMoments.description: A gigantic burning face fills the screen with a tiny Phoenix in front of it, and moments later he fires a beam of light from his orb.

keyMoments.label: Sage's garden
keyMoments.description: The music falls away and Sage walks through a luminous flower garden while her player cradles a handful of glowing flowers.

keyMoments.label: Sage shatters
keyMoments.description: In the second verse, crystals close in around Sage until her face splinters into mirror-like shards.

keyMoments.label: Back on Split: final chorus
keyMoments.description: The music surges back for the final chorus and the video returns to the real round: Phoenix erupts in flame, and Sage heals the wounded Brimstone.

keyMoments.label: Through the fire
keyMoments.description: Chamber lines up another shot as Sage runs up the stairs through a wall of flame, and a revived Phoenix steps back in.

keyMoments.label: The defuse
keyMoments.description: Phoenix throws Sage the defuser, and the defuse finishes in arcs of lightning as agents and players merge.

keyMoments.label: VALORANT Champions Berlin
keyMoments.description: The video closes on the VALORANT Champions logo and the Berlin, December 1–12 date card.

featuredClip.description: A black sun hangs over a blood-red wasteland, a giant Brimstone rises beneath it beside his tiny player and raises his fist, then the sphere plunges into the ground as the beat drops.
